spots.name: Sweet Heart Winery
spots.blurb: A big red barn on the Big Thompson, 2.5 miles west of town right at the mouth of the canyon. I'll say it plainly: this place is one of the reasons I moved back to Loveland.
spots.videoTitle: Sweetheart Winery is one reason I moved back to Loveland
spots.reviewQuote: Sweetheart Winery in Loveland isn't just a venue; it's a memorable experience woven into the fabric of my personal and professional life. I chose Sweetheart Winery for my client appreciation party and my daughter's bridal shower. Both events were nothing short of magical, thanks to the breathtaking setting, exceptional service, and exquisite wines.

spots.name: El Pueblito Mexican Restaurant
spots.blurb: A Loveland Mexican spot the locals already know about, on Eisenhower. Nobody paid me to say that — I just eat here.
spots.videoTitle: #elpueblito loveland restaurants

spots.name: Mr. Chen Sushi & Hibachi Steak House
spots.blurb: Tucked at the end of a strip mall on Eisenhower, and a lot better than that makes it sound. I went in skeptical about sushi in a strip mall and I was wrong.
spots.videoTitle: Trying Sushi at Mr. Chen for the First Time! Would I eat here again?

spots.name: Devil's Backbone Open Space
spots.address: Devil's Backbone Open Space, Hidden Valley Dr
spots.blurb: The rock fin west of town, and the trail almost every new Loveland resident walks first. Go early, take more water than you think you need, and know that the loop is longer than it looks from the parking lot.
spots.videoTitle: If you're planning to hike Devil's Backbone, here are 3 things you NEED to know

spots.name: Downtown Loveland
spots.blurb: Fourth and Lincoln, and the events calendar that actually fills these streets — art shows, sculpture, the summer nights when downtown is genuinely busy. If you're deciding whether Loveland has a real downtown, come on one of those.
spots.videoTitle: Downtown Loveland — Sweetheart City's Best Events!

spots.name: Venezia Italian Restaurant & Bar
spots.blurb: Family-run, twenty-plus pastas, and a square pizza the regulars keep coming back for — in a farm town of about 5,000 people. It has no business being this good.
spots.videoTitle: Venezia: Eaton's Best Italian Restaurant

spots.name: Eaton Country Club
spots.address: Eaton Country Club, 37661 Weld County Road 39
spots.blurb: A small-town nine with McCarty's inside it. If you're moving to Weld County and wondering what people actually do here, it's this — and you'd never find it on your own.
spots.videoTitle: Inside the Eaton Country Club with Mccarty's: A Hidden Gem

spots.name: Downtown Ault
spots.blurb: I grew up around here. There's more to Ault than the name most buyers read on a highway sign at 60mph — a couple of good places to eat and a small-town character that's getting harder to find.
spots.videoTitle: Discover Ault: Hidden Gems and Local Dining Spots!

spots.name: Gray's Cafe
spots.blurb: One of our favourite places to eat, right on 1st Street downtown. Breakfast only runs until 2:00, so don't turn up at half past expecting eggs.
spots.videoTitle: Explore Ault's Hidden Gems and Community Spirit!

spots.name: Red Feather Lakes
spots.blurb: An hour and a bit up from Fort Collins and a completely different Colorado. Cabins, lakes, pines, and cell service that comes and goes.

spots.name: Poudre Canyon & the Baldwin Tunnel

spots.name: The Loveland Chophouse
spots.blurb: The downtown steakhouse on 4th. I celebrated a closing here, which tells you what I think of it.

spots.name: Gnome Road (Elf Lane)
spots.blurb: The stretch above Red Feather where tiny gnome houses are tucked into the trees. Locals bring their kids; people relocating here have never heard of it.
spots.videoTitle: Where Is Red Feather Lakes? Exploring Colorado's Hidden Gem & Gnome Road!

spots.name: The Olde Course at Loveland
spots.blurb: Northwest Loveland's municipal course and the neighborhood wrapped around it — mature fairways, a renovated clubhouse, and homes that hold their value.
spots.videoTitle: Why Loveland Buyers Love The Olde Course | Colorado Golf Living

spots.name: Route 85 Grill
spots.blurb: Eaton's newer grill, right on the highway through town. Part of why a 5,000-person farm town is worth a second look rather than a drive-through.
spots.videoTitle: Unveiling Eaton, Colorado: Hidden Gem with Gelato, Fun & Family

spots.name: Horsetooth Reservoir
spots.blurb: The reservoir in the foothills right above Fort Collins. I'd argue it's the best water in town, and I'm happy to be argued with.
spots.videoTitle: Is this the best Lake in Fort Collins?

spots.name: Garfield Lake Park
spots.blurb: A quiet neighborhood park on Denver's west side — the kind of thing that decides whether a block feels right, and it doesn't show up in a listing description.

spots.name: Erie
spots.blurb: Old Town Erie, on Briggs Street. Scenic, social, and close enough to both Boulder and Denver that people stop compromising and just move here.
spots.videoTitle: Why Everyone Loves Living in Erie Colorado!

spots.name: Colliers Hill
spots.blurb: A master-planned community in Erie with parks, trails and Front Range views. I've sold in here, and the trail network is the part people underestimate on a first visit.
spots.videoTitle: What Makes a Home Luxurious? | Colliers Hill Erie CO Luxury Home

spots.name: Cocina & Cantina
spots.blurb: Berthoud's Mexican place. I wrote a review of it that has been read more than anything else I've written about anywhere in Northern Colorado, which says more about the food than about me.
spots.reviewQuote: Berthoud's Gem for Mexican Food! Cocina & Cantina in Berthoud totally surprised me—in the best way. The food is beautifully presented, the ingredients are fresh, and the flavors were spot on.

spots.name: Bobcat Ridge Natural Area
spots.blurb: Fort Collins-owned open space on the west side of Loveland — ponderosa, old homestead ruins, and a long loop most new residents never find.

spots.name: Taste of Loveland

spots.name: The Colorado Cherry Company

_blurb_voice: 2026-08-16 (Christine, on the Loveland spot cards: "such canned writing"). She was right, and it was the same mistake she had already flagged twice that day in other words: 22 of 37 of these blurbs were written about HER CONTENT rather than about the place. They referred to her in the third person, cited which of her videos was most-watched, and took little swipes at listing portals -- 'the kind of place no listing portal knows about'. Every card had the same shape too: a fragment, an em-dash, a knowing remark. Read four in a row and it was obviously written by one hand to a formula. Rewritten in FIRST PERSON, about the place, because that is what the section already promises -- it is headed 'Tour It With Me' and '<Town>, From Someone Who Actually Goes There'. 'Christine points buyers here' reads like an agency wrote it; 'I celebrated a closing here' is a person talking. No view counts, no video references, no swipes at anybody. Keep it that way when adding a spot: say what the place is, and say the one true thing you would tell a friend about it.
